title: Counterintuitive inverse superconducting transition beyond 4He-cooling limit
authors: Haowen Han, Yi Bian, Tong Ma, Yusong Zhao, Nuofu Chen, Chuanying Xi, Ze Wang, Binghui Ge, Hongliang Dong, Jia-Cai Nie, Ho-Kwang Mao, Jikun Chen
abstract: Thermally driven quantum-orders observed in exceptional instances may redefine the role of thermal-fluctuation from a source of decoherence to a resource for coherent-state engineering. While preliminary signs of counterintuitive temperature-rise-triggered superconductivity manifested in CeCu2Si2, ErRh4B4, Ho1.2Mo6S8 and (La,Ce)Al2, their critical-temperatures (Tc-inv) remain below Kelvin-range, precluding substantial applications. Here, we report field-modulated inverse-superconducting-transitions above 4He-cooling-limit in Eu-based infinite-layer nickelates (EuxNd1-xNiO2 and EuxPr1-xNiO2) grown on a substrate under both overdoped and underdoped regimes. Paradigmatically, superconductivity with zero-resistance is confined between Tc-inv (2.6-5.4 K) and another higher normal-Tc, rising and decreasing with applied magnetic-field, respectively. Starting from the resistive-state below Tc-inv, the inverse-superconducting-transition is driven by not only temperature-rising, but also current-density, while superconductivity further vanishes at higher temperature and current thresholds. The Kelvin-range inverse superconducting transition is plausibly explained by temperature-induced alternating dominance of effective magnetic-fields arising from Eu2+4f7 related compensations relative to the upper-critical-field. Furthermore, an extended-phenomenological-framework is also supported by reemerged superconductivity below 300 mK under magnetic-field, giving rise to an unprecedented temperature-induced reentrant superconductivity. Our findings establish magnetic-interaction-reconfigured high-Tc systems as fertile platforms for exploring quantum phenomena that reverse thermal-decoherence paradigm, also enabling antithetical-designs to unlock untapped application-scenarios for quantum-phase-transition devices.
summary: The authors report discovering an inverse superconducting transition—where superconductivity appears upon heating—in Eu-doped nickelates. They demonstrate this effect persists above the 4He cooling limit using high magnetic fields and current injection. This work suggests that complex magnetic interactions can fundamentally alter the thermal stability of quantum superconducting phases.
main_problem: The research investigates counterintuitive superconducting transitions, specifically superconductivity induced by an *increase* in temperature (inverse transition), moving beyond previously observed limits.
main_result: They report observing field-modulated inverse superconducting transitions above the 4He-cooling limit in Eu-based infinite-layer nickelates, suggesting a mechanism involving temperature-induced magnetic field dominance.
method: The study relies on detailed transport measurements, including resistivity vs. temperature ($ho$-$T$), resistivity vs. magnetic field ($ho$-$H$), and current-voltage ($I$-$V$) characteristics under high fields.
model_or_system: The physical platform is Eu-doped infinite-layer nickelates (e.g., $	ext{EuxNd}_{1-x}	ext{NiO}_2$). The behavior is analyzed by comparing measured effective magnetic fields to theoretical upper critical fields, deviating from standard Jaccarino-Peter compensation models.
key_observables: Zero-resistance state boundaries ($T_{c	ext{-inv}}$ and $T_c$), field dependence ($ho$-$H$ cross-linking), current density triggering of transitions, and reemerged superconductivity at sub-Kelvin temperatures.
important_parameters: Magnetic fields up to 35 T; temperature ranges spanning from $\sim 60 	ext{ mK}$ to several Kelvin; doping levels (overdoped/underdoped regimes).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the inverse transition is governed by an alternating dominance of effective magnetic fields related to Eu$^{2+}$ compensations relative to $H_{c2}$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $ho$-$T$ curves showing the characteristic inverse superconducting dome, high-field phase diagrams mapping the boundaries between normal and superconducting states, and $I$-$V$ characteristics demonstrating current-induced transitions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents evidence for the unusual superconducting phase diagram, first establishing the existence of the inverse transition ($T_{c	ext{-inv}}$), then detailing its field and current dependence, and finally proposing a mechanism based on magnetic field compensation effects.
why_interesting: This work explores non-equilibrium quantum phenomena in strongly correlated materials where thermal fluctuations are not purely decohering but can actively engineer superconducting states, which is highly relevant to understanding exotic pairing mechanisms beyond BCS theory.
